questions.stem: A 3-year-old child was brought to the ER with metabolic acidosis after accidental ingestion of flavoured aspirin tablets of an unknown quantity. Her blood pH - 7.0, pKa of aspirin - 3, calculate the ratio of its ionized to unionized forms at the same pH 7.0.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. 10,000 to 1

 

Option B:

 

This question requires application of the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation to determine the ratio of ionized to unionized forms of aspirin at a given pH.

 

The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation is: pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA])

 

Where:

  • [A⁻] represents the concentration of the ionized (deprotonated) form
  • [HA] represents the concentration of the unionized (protonated) form

 

Given:

  • pH = 7.0
  • pKa of aspirin = 3.0

 

 

Log 101 = 1

Log 102 = 2

Log 103 = 3

Log 104 = 4

 

So, the ratio of ionized to unionized aspirin is 10,000:1 at pH 7.

 

Educational Objective:

 

"The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation permits calculation of the ratio of ionized to unionized species for a weak acid at any given pH."

 

Ref: Lippincott 7/e: p 6-10.

questions.stem: In a renal physiology session, medical residents are discussing various methods to evaluate kidney function. One resident mentions a substance used in a specific clearance test that accurately measures the glomerular filtration rate (GFR), which is essential for assessing renal function. The residents are asked to identify the substance used in this gold-standard test for GFR assessment. Which of the following substances is used to measure GFR through its clearance rate?
questions.solutionHtml:
e="font-size:12.0pt">Explanation:

 

Option A. Creatinine: While creatinine clearance is commonly used in clinical practice to estimate GFR due to its practicality, it is not as accurate as inulin clearance because creatinine is slightly secreted by the renal tubules in addition to being filtered by the glomerulus.

 

Option B. Urea: Urea clearance is not an accurate measure of GFR because urea is both reabsorbed and secreted by the renal tubules.

 

Option D. Albumin: Albumin is a large protein that is normally not filtered by the glomerulus in significant amounts due to its size and charge; thus, it is not used to measure GFR.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Inulin is a polysaccharide of fructose and is not appreciably metabolized by the body.
  • It is neither absorbed nor secreted by the tubules →Hence, it is a measure of GFR.
  • The value of GFR as measured by inulin clearance is 125 mL/min.

 

Ref: DM Vasudevan 9/e: p 418.

questions.stemHtml: In the outpatient department, three patients suspected of having dysglycemia underwent an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). Their plasma glucose levels were measured at intervals after glucose ingestion, as depicted in the graph. Based on their glucose level trends, which patient most likely represents a pre-diabetic state?
questions.solutionHtml:
pt;">The correct answer is: C. Patient 2

 

Explanation:

 

Pre-diabetes (also called impaired glucose tolerance) is characterized by blood glucose levels that are higher than normal but not high enough to be classified as diabetes. In an OGTT, pre-diabetes typically shows:

  • Fasting glucose that may be slightly elevated (100-125 mg/dL)
  • A 2-hour post-load glucose between 140-199 mg/dL

 

 

Analyzing each patient:

 

Patient 1 (red squares):

  • Starting glucose ~90 mg/dL (normal fasting)
  • Returns to ~100 mg/dL by 120 min
  • This represents a normal glucose tolerance pattern

 

Patient 2 (blue triangles):

  • Starting glucose ~80 mg/dL
  • Slow decline but remains elevated at ~145 mg/dL at 120 min
  • This pattern shows impaired glucose tolerance (pre-diabetes) with delayed return to normal

 

Patient 3 (green circles):

  • Starting glucose ~140 mg/dL (already elevated at fasting)
  • Remains very elevated at 120 min (~210 mg/dL)
  • This pattern is consistent with diabetes mellitus

 

Patient 2 best represents pre-diabetes because their fasting level is normal but they show impaired glucose tolerance with the 2-hour value remaining elevated at ~145 mg/d.

 

Educational Objective :


The OGTT is used to assess how well the body clears glucose from the bloodstream. In a pre-diabetic state, the 2-hour glucose value is elevated beyond normal but does not reach diabetic levels (140–199 mg/dL). If the value is ≥200 mg/dL, a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus is made.

 

Ref: Harper 30/e p 337 -340.

questions.stem: A patient with a known history of diabetes mellitus presents to the outpatient department for a routine follow-up appointment after three months. As part of the management and monitoring plan, the healthcare provider requests an HbA1c test, which is crucial for assessing long-term glycemic control. Considering the various methods available for HbA1c estimation, which of the following is considered the most accurate and reliable method?
questions.solutionHtml:

    Explanation:

     

    Option A. Affinity chromatography: While affinity chromatography can be used for HbA1c measurement, it is not as specific or as widely used as HPLC. It relies on the specific binding of HbA1c to a particular substrate, which can be influenced by the presence of hemoglobin variants.

     

    Option B.  Electrophoresis: Electrophoresis can separate different hemoglobin types based on their electric charge, but it is less precise than HPLC for quantifying HbA1c levels and can be affected by the presence of hemoglobin variants.

HPLC separates various forms of hemoglobin, including HbA1c, based on their charge and size under high pressure, allowing for precise quantification. questions.stem: In individuals experiencing hemolysis, the long-term control of blood sugar levels cannot be accurately assessed using glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) due to the shortened lifespan of red blood cells. Instead, another biomarker must be utilized. Fructosamine, which refers to glycated serum proteins such as albumin, has been suggested as an alternative measure. Is the statement that fructosamine is a glycated albumin true or false?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) True.

 

Option A:

 

  • Along with other proteins, albumin is also glycated in diabetes mellitus.
  • Glycated albumin is called fructosamine albumin.
  • As half-life of albumin is 20 days, gluco-albumin concentration reflects the glucose control over the last 2-3 weeks.
  • Estimation of serum fructosamine is preferred in gestational diabetes mellitus.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Fructosamine is a measure of glycemic control that can be used as an alternative to HbA1c, particularly in situations where red blood cell turnover is increased, such as hemolysis. It specifically reflects the glycation of serum proteins like albumin over a shorter time frame.
